correctness.rationale: Since P=[-omega r,-omega(r-omega Ar)] with omega>0, its range is exactly span{r,Ar}. x_pre-x=omega r lies in the same range, so the residual-minimizing correction solves the identical affine trial-space problem as GMRES(2), independent of the weight. Independence of r and Ar plus invertibility of A implies Ar,A²r independent and G positive definite. Direct Gram expansion gives entries omega²[u,u-omega v;u-omega v,u-2omega v+omega²w], determinant omega^6 Delta>0, trace omega²(2u-2omega v+omega²w). For eigenvalue ratio kappa≥1, T=trace/sqrt(det)=sqrt(kappa)+1/sqrt(kappa) is strictly increasing in kappa. Consequently T=(2u/omega-2v+w omega)/sqrt(Delta) and its completed-square difference from T_star is w(omega-omega_star)²/(omega sqrt(Delta)); this proves one strict global optimum over omega>0. T_star=2 precisely when v=sqrt(uw/2); can verify by squaring in |v|<sqrt(uw). As T tends to infinity at both ends, kappa~T², giving the two claimed sharp asymptotics. Each next cycle has same identity when the pair remains independent, and an eigenvector or zero residual is excluded/terminating. Independent exact Fraction implementation of a different two-column residual projection verified 1399 assertions for 45 nonsingular 3x3 systems with seven omega values, including nonsymmetric systems. A 2x2 explicit equality case gave G=I and the 3x3 SPD stability-interval example gave 2u/w=835/428. These finite tests are corroboration only.

value.rationale: This specific two-grid accelerator has two physically meaningful choices that are often conflated: the scalar smoother weight and the arithmetic conditioning of the coarse solve. The theorem establishes an exact search-space invariance across all positive weights while isolating a unique best-conditioned coarse normal system, a strict penalty for deviation, a realizable perfect-conditioning equality case and sharp quadratic degeneration at the weight extremes. For a natural recently introduced numerical method, identifying a free algorithmic parameter with no exact iteration effect but a precisely quantifiable normal-matrix conditioning effect is independently useful for fair comparisons, benchmarking and parameter selection. The optimum can lie outside the conventional standalone Richardson stability interval, a substantive implementation caveat. No unsupported claim of faster finite-precision performance or general solver convergence is made.

final_claim: For every real nonsingular n×n A, n≥2, and nonzero r=b-Ax for which r,Ar are independent, the depth-one TGA(1;1,0) with scalar positive Richardson smoothing B=omega I, exact residual-minimizing A^T A projection and columns P=[-omega r,-omega(r-omega Ar)] yields exactly the two-step restarted GMRES cycle from x for every omega>0 (on each nondegenerate cycle). The corresponding normal Gram G=P^T A^T A P has a unique positive spectral-condition-number optimum omega_star=sqrt(2u/w), u=||Ar||²,w=||A²r||²; T(trace/sqrt(det)) has exact penalty w(omega-omega_star)²/(omega sqrt(Delta)), Delta=uw-(Ar·A²r)²>0. Perfect conditioning iff Ar·A²r=sqrt(uw/2); kappa_2(G)~4u²/(Delta omega²) as omega↓0 and ~w² omega²/Delta as omega→∞. No finite precision or global convergence claims.
